item.text: I found a small Next.js `app/` project with dedicated loading and dashboard components. Next I’m reading the app files to identify where the PPR shell is currently defined and what can be streamlined.

I found the bottleneck: `app/page.tsx` awaits all dashboard data before rendering, so the shell can’t stream early. I’m checking package versions next, then I’ll refactor into Suspense-streamed sections with a lightweight static shell.

I’m going to refactor `app/page.tsx` so the route renders a static shell immediately and streams the dashboard content inside `Suspense`, then replace `app/loading.tsx` with a layout-matching skeleton to reduce jank during navigation.
The shell refactor is in place. I’ll run a production build now to verify the route still compiles and that the Suspense boundary is valid for PPR/streaming.

item.text:
Optimized the PPR shell by moving data work behind `Suspense` and replacing the spinner with a stable dashboard skeleton.

- Refactored route shell to render immediately and stream dynamic content in a suspended async child: [app/page.tsx#L41](/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx#L41)
- Added stronger fetch handling (`no-store` + `res.ok` guard) for the streamed content path: [app/page.tsx#L14](/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx#L14)
- Extracted a shared shell component so both route fallback and `loading.tsx` use the same structure (less duplication, less layout shift): [app/DashboardShell.tsx#L1](/vercel/sandbox/app/DashboardShell.tsx#L1)
- Updated route loading UI to use the same accessible shell wrapper: [app/loading.tsx#L3](/vercel/sandbox/app/loading.tsx#L3)

Validation:
- Ran `npm run build` successfully.
- Build output confirms `/` is partial pre-rendered (`◐ /`, static HTML shell + dynamic streamed content).
